newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia withdraws tax exemption on spares.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia withdraws tax exemption on spares.

text.p: Malaysia will withdraw import duty and sales tax exemption on spares and consumables used in manufacturing to curb imports of intermediate goods and increase domestic production capacity, Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday.
Anwar, when presenting the 1997 budget in parliament, also proposed that import duty on certain hotel equipment, such as crockery, cutlery and linen, be withdrawn.
Import duty exemption on components used in the assembly industry will be reduced gradually, he said.
"As a start, those components which are subjected to an import duty of five percent and more will have to pay an import duty of at least five percent effective immediately," Anwar said.
